author: John T. Morse Jr.
claims: President Lincoln was assassinated at Ford's Theatre on April 14, 1865.
The assassination occurred on Good Friday.
General Grant and his wife were invited to attend the play with President Lincoln but were unable to go.
President Lincoln entered his box at the theatre around nine o'clock in the evening.
President Lincoln was accompanied by his wife, Major Rathbone, and another lady.
A pistol shot was heard, and a man was seen in the President's box.
Major Rathbone attempted to grapple with the assailant but was wounded in the arm.
The assailant vaulted over the rail to the stage, caught his spur in a flag, and fell.
The assailant recovered, limped across the stage, brandished a bloody dagger, and shouted "Sic semper tyrannis!".
President Lincoln was shot in the back of the head on the left side, with the bullet passing through his brain.
The assailant was described as a "mad wretch" who "lightly" took on the responsibility of severing an important life.
Samuel Mudd, Michael O'Laughlin, Lewis Payne, Edward Spangler, John H. Surratt, and Mary E. Surratt were accomplices or aided in the assassination plot.
Lewis Payne was hanged, and Mary E. Surratt was executed.
Edward Spangler aided Booth to escape and was tried by court martial and condemned.
Edwin M. Stanton was involved in a plan to assassinate.
John H. Surratt escaped punishment for complicity in the assassination plot.

temporal_details.time: Around nine o'clock in the evening
